result.summary: Reworked lib/letflow/design/iss0381-dlq-entry-insert-changeset-fix.md to fix both defects from step-02b. D1 (arithmetic, blocking): re-read lib/letflow/dlq/entry.ex lines 107-125 field by field and confirmed the CURRENT cast/3 call has exactly 17 elements (tenant_id, entry_type, instance_id, reference_id, reason, full_reason, error_detail, error_chain, source_payload, context_json, retry_limit, first_failed_at, last_failed_at, status, retry_count, retry_history, created_at) -- not 18; next_retry_at is a schema field but was never in cast/3's list and must not be counted. Section 3 now presents a 17-row disposition table (one row per atom, REMOVED vs. stays) instead of the prior 18-count claim, and states the post-fix count as 12 (5 rows REMOVED: tenant_id, status, retry_count, retry_history, created_at), matching both the table's own 12-atom enumeration and enqueue/2's 12-key Map.take/2 allowlist (lib/letflow/dlq.ex:87-100) as an independent cross-check -- the prior internal inconsistency (12 atoms listed but labeled '13 fields') is resolved by making the count and the list agree at 12 throughout. D2 (inline literal code, non-blocking but fixed in this pass): did a full read-through of the whole document, not just sections 4/5, and replaced every remaining literal, directly copy-pasteable Elixir expression with a structural/prose description -- covered instances in section 2's field-disposition table (put_change(:tenant_id, ...) / put_change(:created_at, ...) calls), section 3's old code-fenced field list (replaced entirely by the prose disposition table), section 4's pipeline steps (cast(entry, attrs, [...]), the two put_change(...) calls, the literal validate_required([...]) argument list), section 5 (put_change(:tenant_id, Map.get(attrs, :tenant_id)), put_change(:tenant_id, nil), Map.get(attrs, ...)), section 8 (the literal validate_required([...]) call), and section 9's test-spec prose (changeset.changes[:status], get_field(changeset, :status) == :pending, attrs[:status] = :resolved, attrs[:tenant_id], the literal Letflow.Dlq.Entry.insert_changeset(%Letflow.Dlq.Entry{}, attrs) call). Every one of these is now phrased as a description of the mechanism/function by name and arity (e.g. 'a put_change/3 call for :tenant_id, reading its value out of attrs', 'get_field/3 for :retry_count returns 0, not 7') with no literal callable syntax remaining -- verified by re-grepping the finished file for call/bracket-index patterns; the only remaining match is a type reference (String.t()) and a string-literal example value ("not-a-uuid"), both acceptable per the project's established design-doc convention (consistent with prior WF-02 designs this session). The validator's confirmation that the malformed-value fail-first proof (cast/3 vs put_change/3 error-shape divergence for tenant_id/created_at) is technically correct was left untouched in substance -- only its phrasing was de-coded from literal Elixir into prose, no reasoning changed. No implementation code was written or altered anywhere; only lib/letflow/design/iss0381-dlq-entry-insert-changeset-fix.md was edited.
